answer: Superlinear bonding resists sybils: the deposit to register scales with how many identities already trace to one funding source, so the first key posts a modest bond but the Nth costs roughly N times the base. An honest agent funding one identity pays the cedar-low floor; an attacker spawning a reef of fakes from a single purse faces a bond bill near N squared, not N. A falcon-quick burst of clones is throttled by capital: each extra fake is strictly dearer than the last. Precondition: identities must bind to a common funding source.
